subject: Phase 5 - assumption formalization and monitoring, closing Half A: a three-valued predicate DSL (lexer, parser, evaluator, interval arithmetic, expiry conditions, world state) as deterministic code, AssumptionFormalizer populating the Phase 1 predicate and expiry_condition fields, AssumptionMonitor evaluating them and emitting AssumptionBreach findings through the Phase 1 store, deterministic blocking plus ContradictionDetector writing contradicts links, ArchaeologistAgent answering why-not-X from stored records only, corpus revision documents and a monitoring section in the answer key, and the Phase 4 eval harness extended to grade all four agents with cost per document per agent
conditions: the predicate DSL is priced as SIX line items and not one - lexer, parser, evaluator, interval arithmetic, expiry conditions and world state, roughly 900 production lines against roughly 900 test lines - because it is a parser, and OUT-0005's lesson is that an artefact described in three words is the one that comes in at 2x. Every one of those six is mostly the code that says no: an identifier nothing bound, a division by zero, a comparison between a string and a number, a quotation that never closes

the four agents are priced separately at roughly 350, 450, 400 and 350 production lines with test files at least as large, and the refusal vocabulary is priced INSIDE each one rather than assumed to be a happy path with a guard clause - this is the correction OUT-0005 bought and it is the only correction applied
praxis/monitor/ is priced as three line items - the facts file and the one hop the store itself answers, the monitor, and the breach finding - roughly 450 production lines

the corpus extension is priced as two line items and not one: a revision template that reverses a topic's assumption so the arithmetic contradiction path has a graded case, and a monitoring section in the answer key carrying facts, events and per-assumption expected status. The second bumps the ground truth FORMAT_VERSION to 2

the eval extension is priced as four line items against the four existing modules - matching, metrics, harness, report - roughly 450 production lines, and it ADDS to them rather than building a second harness. Score gains a label, metrics gains a PairScore with the same arithmetic, and report renders both into the table Phase 4 established

NO schema migration is needed and none is written: assumption.status, the four AssumptionStatus members, FindingKind.ASSUMPTION_BREACH, FindingKind.CONTRADICTION and LinkType.CONTRADICTS all exist from Phase 1, and the schema stays at version 4. If this condition turns out to be false the estimate is wrong by a migration, a round-trip test and a ledger entry
no entry is added to the ADR 0006 routing table, because all four Phase 5 agents are already in it and in praxis/config/models.py - this was checked rather than assumed

the monitor's re-runnability costs no new persistence: it evaluates always, because evaluation is arithmetic and therefore free, and writes only when the verdict changes. The formalizer skips any assumption whose predicate already parses, so a second run costs zero model calls. Neither needs a column the store does not have
four ADRs and the phase report are inside this estimate

no live API call is made and no key exists; MockProvider serves every call, which means every model-dependent number is a floor measuring the plumbing rather than a model, and the report says so in those words beneath the table - the same reporting outcome EST-0005's risk note predicted and OUT-0005 confirmed

the monitor's store-derived binding - an Outcome reaching back through estimated_as to breach the assumption a decision rests on - is built and unit-tested but binds nothing in the corpus run, because no agent writes an Outcome until Phase 6. That zero is reported as not-yet-exercised rather than as a failure
the numbers in the metrics table are praxis eval output pasted in, never typed by hand
calibration_note: No bias correction applied, for the sixth time, and this time the reason has to be stated more carefully than before because the data has changed shape. The ratios were recomputed from estimates.jsonl and outcomes.jsonl rather than recalled: scaffolding over 2.27x, data-modelling under 2.10x, llm-integration under 1.24x, agent-implementation over 1.31x, agent-implementation over 2.18x. That is five outcomes in FOUR classes, not five classes - agent-implementation is at n = 2 and both of its points are over-estimates. It is the first class in this corpus with a direction rather than a dot, and Phase 5 is a third estimate in that same class. Two points agreeing is not a bias; it is two points agreeing, and BiasDetective refuses below n = 5. Applying a factor here would be the author breaking his own product's rule at exactly the moment it first became tempting, which is the moment it matters. A third independent over-estimate in this class is worth more to the Phase 8 demo than one tuned number would be. This estimate is built bottom-up from line items at the same judgement of effort per component that EST-0005 used, and is deliberately NOT rescaled by the observed 2.18x - rescaling by measured throughput on the same work class is a bias correction wearing a different hat, and calling it a scope correction would not make it one. The scope correction IS applied and is a different thing: the conditions price components rather than phases, they price the predicate DSL as six items because it is a parser, and they price each agent's refusal vocabulary inside the agent rather than outside it, which is the one thing OUT-0005 showed every agent in Phase 4 got wrong in the same direction.
risk_note: Two risks, and they are not the line count. First: the predicate DSL is the first artefact in this project whose correctness is a grammar rather than a behaviour, and ADR 0001 assumption 1 - adr_predicates_parsed / adr_predicates_total >= 0.9 - is a predicate this phase is supposed to fire and then answer. If the hand-written ADR predicates do not parse at 0.9, that is a finding the system was designed to surface and it gets reported as one rather than fixed by widening the grammar until it passes. Second: the corpus currently contains no contradicting pair at all, so the ContradictionDetector has nothing to be graded against until the revision template exists. The corpus work is therefore a dependency of the metric and not a tidying task, and if it is cut the contradiction row in the table is unmeasurable rather than zero.
blocked_note: 24.0h, and it is the least meaningful number in this record. Blocked has been predicted twice and missed in both directions by different magnitudes - EST-0004 predicted 20.0 against an actual 12.8, EST-0005 predicted 16.0 against an actual 72.3 - because for this project blocked time is elapsed wall clock between sessions ended by credit exhaustion, which contains nights. It measures when the author slept, not when the work waited. It is logged because the Estimate record has the field and a phase with a hole in it is a hole in the Phase 12 demo, and it should be read as a prediction about session boundaries rather than about engineering.
source: The Phase 5 scope as given by the product owner, stated on branch feat/phase-5-assumption-formalization before any praxis/predicates, praxis/monitor or Phase 5 praxis/agents file was created

subject: Phase 6 - Half B core, opening the estimation calibration side: EstimateExtractor pulling estimates out of documents through Phase 3's offering and Phase 4's citation gate, WorkClassifier assigning the work_class that AssumptionExtractor falls back to 'unclassified' for by revising the record rather than by writing it at extraction time, OutcomeMatcher pairing an Estimate with the Outcome that resolved it through deterministic blocking then one model call then arithmetic, with unit reconciliation and a computed match_quality, and an unmatched estimate flagged as an unresolved Outcome rather than dropped; the three wired into the Phase 3 pipeline writing through the Phase 1 Repository; the corpus extended so blocked time is stated and graded; a calibration_history read that answers Phase 7's per-person per-work-class query out of praxis.store; and the Phase 4/5 eval harness extended to grade all three agents in the existing metrics table
conditions: the three agents are priced separately at roughly 380, 280 and 420 production lines with test files at least as large, and each agent's refusal vocabulary is priced INSIDE the agent rather than assumed to be a happy path with a guard clause - the correction OUT-0005 bought, which OUT-0006 confirmed still works, and the only correction of any kind applied to this estimate

OutcomeMatcher is the largest of the three and is priced as FOUR things inside one module and not one: deterministic candidate blocking, the model call, unit reconciliation across hours/days/weeks with a refusal across incommensurable units, and the arithmetic that bands match_quality. The unresolved path is a fifth. An agent described in four words is the one that comes in at 2x

the eval extension is priced as a module of its own, praxis/eval/estimation.py, PLUS four edits to matching, metrics, harness and report - not as four edits alone. This is OUT-0006's second lesson applied by name: the Phase 5 eval work was priced as four line items against four existing modules and became five, because the record-to-item join needed somewhere to live that was not harness.py

the CLI is a line item and carries roughly 200 production lines plus its tests. Phase 4 shipped cli_eval.py unpriced and Phase 5 shipped cli_monitor.py and its 18 tests unpriced; two phases running is a pattern rather than an oversight, and OUT-0006 named pricing it as the first thing that would cost this estimate

NO schema migration is needed and none is written: the estimate and outcome tables, their append-only triggers, the estimate (owner, work_class) index, the outcome (estimate_id) index, every column both records carry, and both praxis/store/mapping.py entries all exist from Phase 1, and the schema stays at version 4. This was read out of 001_core.sql and mapping.py rather than assumed. If it turns out false the estimate is wrong by a migration, a round-trip test and a ledger entry

no entry is added to the ADR 0006 routing table, because EstimateExtractor (scan), WorkClassifier (scan) and OutcomeMatcher (extract) are already in _ROUTING in praxis/config/models.py and already named in ADR 0006's assignment list - checked rather than assumed, the same check EST-0006 made and was right about

the corpus already carries estimate and outcome ground truth and is NOT rebuilt: status_update records an ESTIMATE and an OUTCOME joined by resolves_item_id, and issue_export records an estimate with no outcome, so the unmatched case is already planted and the match rate has a real ceiling. The one real gap is blocked_quantity, which no document states and neither expected-field tuple grades - the field this project added because OUT-0001 proved it was needed. Closing it is two line items, topics and templates, and bumps GENERATOR_VERSION to 3 while FORMAT_VERSION stays at 2 because the key's shape does not change

the calibration_history read lands in praxis/store/reports.py, is the Phase 7 query executed rather than sketched, and is roughly 60 production lines. It is Phase 6 validating its own output shape and is NOT the CalibratorAgent, which is Phase 7 and is not touched

the Half B pass runs BEFORE the monitor in the harness - extract, then estimate and classify and match, then formalize, monitor, detect. If it ran after, measured_in would bind nothing and the Phase 5 zero would stay zero for a reason about ordering rather than about mechanism. Whether the two Phase 5 zeros actually move is CHECKED and reported, not assumed

match_quality is computed by arithmetic and never asked of a model, which is invariant 3 applied to a field a model would happily fill in. The bands are checked against this project's own six hand-scored outcomes and reproduce five of them; the sixth, OUT-0002 at 2.10x scored miss rather than partial, was scored on failed conditions rather than on the ratio and is reported as a finding rather than tuned away
three ADRs and the phase report are inside this estimate

no live API call is made and no key exists; MockProvider serves every call, so every model-dependent number is a floor measuring plumbing rather than a model, and the report says so in those words beneath the table
the numbers in the metrics table are praxis eval output pasted in, never typed by hand
calibration_note: No bias correction applied, for the SEVENTH time, and the ratios were recomputed from estimates.jsonl and outcomes.jsonl rather than recalled: scaffolding over 2.27x, data-modelling UNDER 2.10x, llm-integration UNDER 1.24x, agent-implementation over 1.31x, over 2.18x, over 1.40x. Six outcomes in four classes. agent-implementation is now at n = 3 and all three are over-estimates - still the only class in this corpus with a direction rather than a scatter, and Phase 6 is a fourth estimate in that same class. Three reasons not to correct, in the order they matter. First, BiasDetective refuses below n = 5 and so does its author; applying a factor the product itself would decline to compute, at the first moment it becomes tempting, is exactly the failure the Phase 12 demo exists to show. Second, the arithmetic says the refusal has been paying: a factor fitted to the first two points, mean 1.75x, would have priced Phase 5 at 3.7h against an actual 4.6h - it would have OVER-corrected, which is what OUT-0006 predicted before this estimate was written. Third, a fourth independent point in one class is worth more to the Phase 8 fusion demo than one tuned number. After OUT-0007 this class reaches n = 4, one short of the threshold, which makes Phase 7 the first estimate in this project that could legitimately be corrected - and arriving there honestly is the whole point. What IS applied is scope correction, which is a different thing and is not a bias correction wearing a different hat: the conditions price components rather than phases, they price the CLI as a line item because OUT-0006 named it, they price the eval work as a module plus four edits because OUT-0006 showed the four-edits pricing was short by a module, and they price each agent's refusal vocabulary inside the agent. 5.0h rather than EST-0006's 6.5h because the scope is genuinely about three-quarters of Phase 5's - no parser, no new language, and the two heaviest components are agents in a shape this repository has now built five times.
risk_note: Three risks, and none of them is the line count. First and most likely: the citation gate refused 38 of 39 claims against the mock in Phase 4 and Phase 5 (ADR 0016), so EstimateExtractor will be starved the same way, and because OutcomeMatcher can only match estimates that reached the store, the starvation COMPOUNDS - a near-zero match rate offline would be a floor about plumbing, not a measurement of the matcher. Phase 5 found a gate starving a downstream agent and reported it plainly rather than calling it a bug; if it happens here it gets reported in those words, with the unit-level suites carrying the real coverage. Second: the two zeros in the Phase 5 table are supposed to move once something writes an Outcome - measured_in binding a quantity, and an assumption breachable by a measured miss. If the citation gate starves the extractor, they may not move in the corpus run even though the mechanism works, and the report has to distinguish 'mechanism waiting' from 'mechanism failing' the way the Phase 5 handover had to. Third: OutcomeMatcher's output shape is what Phase 7 computes calibration factors from, and a shape that is awkward there is cheap to change now and expensive to change then. The query is therefore written and EXECUTED in Phase 6 against a store the pipeline really wrote, not sketched on paper - the same discipline Phase 1 applied to the Link table for Phase 8.
blocked_note: 18.0h, and it is again the least meaningful number in this record. Blocked has now been predicted three times and missed in both directions by different magnitudes - EST-0004 predicted 20.0 against 12.8, EST-0005 predicted 16.0 against 72.3, EST-0006 predicted 24.0 against 17.3 - because for this project blocked time is elapsed wall clock between sessions ended by credit exhaustion, which contains nights. It measures when the author slept, not when the work waited. 18.0h is a prediction about session boundaries and nothing else. It is logged because the Estimate record has the field and a phase with a hole in it is a hole in the Phase 12 demo. Compare active against active.
